summary: Real, live defect in main (HEAD fcd5bc0): on a seeded webapp repair cell the agent lands and in-run verifies the fix 20/20 but the harness records 11/20 runs as `exhausted`. I reproduced the 9-complete/11-exhausted split directly from the 20 JSONL records and traced the mechanism end-to-end in askme.py. The loss is the consecutive-duplicate shell guard: a second consecutive re-run of an already-successful verification command hard-terminates the whole task attempt (`END_ATTEMPT`) before the executor can ever select `done`, so the task is marked `task_failed`, replans burn out, and the run falls through to `exhausted`. One material correction to the issue body: its trace claim that "`done` is emitted zero times in all 20 runs" is false — it is an instrumentation artifact, because an accepted `done` is counted by `recorder.selected()` but never produces a `step` or `step_skipped` JSONL event. In all 9 complete runs the residual (selected − executed − skipped) exactly equals `completed_tasks`, and 8 of the 11 exhausted runs also emitted accepted `done`s.

Therefore every `task_complete` in these records REQUIRED an accepted `done`. The records agree: residual = selected − executed − skipped equals `completed_tasks` in all 9 complete runs (1/1, 2/2, 3/3, 3/3, 3/3, 2/2, 2/2, 2/2, 2/2). Root cause of the miscount: `_handle_done` (askme.py:4560-4568) calls neither `recorder.executed()` nor `recorder.skip()` and emits no `_event`, so an ACCEPTED done is invisible in JSONL, while REFUSED dones are recorded (`lifecycle_unverified_done` askme.py:3394, `incomplete_write_done` askme.py:3516).

(2) CLAIM "the duplicate/stuck guards suppress that command because it already succeeded → task cannot be satisfied → task_failed → replan → exhaustion" — CONFIRMED, with a sharper mechanism than the issue states. askme.py:3113-3130:
```
elif act == "shell" and prev.get("arg", "") == action.get("arg", ""):
    if prev.get("ok"):

            controller.state["errors"].append(
                f"[stuck_loop] shell {action.get('arg','')[:60]}: same successful command repeated")
            controller.recorder.skip(ctx.task_index, ctx.step, act, action, "stuck_shell_repeat")
            return _StepFlow.END_ATTEMPT
```
`END_ATTEMPT` returns out of `_run_attempt` (askme.py:4432-4433) with `attempt.done` still False, so `_run_task` returns done=False (askme.py:4421), `_execute_tasks` emits `task_failed` and `break`s (askme.py:4309-4320), `all_done` is False so `self.completion.try_finish(replan)` at askme.py:4176 is never reached.

(3) EXACT SITE where a landed, verified repair is recorded exhausted: askme.py:4171-4181 —
```
for replan in range(self.max_replans):
    tasks = self._plan(replan)
    if tasks is None: continue
    if self._execute_tasks(tasks):
        outcome = self.completion.try_finish(replan)
        if outcome is not None: break
if outcome is None:
    outcome = self.completion.exhausted()      # askme.py:4180
```
with the status string built at askme.py:3850 (`self._build_outcome("exhausted", validation, controller.max_replans)`); the docstring at askme.py:3840-3846 says exhaustion is now reported "unconditionally" precisely so a budget burn can never be laundered into success. The workspace state (repaired app.py, passing test) is never consulted at this site.

(4) The unidentified mediator the issue asks about (#1 in its investigation list) has a concrete code-level candidate the issue does not name: the guard only compares against the IMMEDIATELY previous step (askme.py:3020-3022, `if not last or last[0]["action"] != act: return None; prev = last[0]`), and `attempt.dup_skip_count = 0` is reset on ANY executed action (askme.py:4573). So the run dies only if the model emits the same successful shell TWICE IN A ROW with nothing dispatched between. That is a stochastic, gradual property of the model's action interleaving — exactly matching the issue's "race" description and its finding that raw suppression counts do not discriminate (suppression occurs in 20/20 runs including all 9 that complete).

THREE LANES:
1. macos-tests — GATES. runs-on: macos-26 (free hosted M1 arm64). Matrix Python 3.10 and 3.14. MODEL: none at all — it never sets ASKME_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS, so conftest.py keeps both backend suites skipped; hermetic by construction. 3. llama-reference — GATES (including a hard runner-size floor), but is `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` — manual only, deliberately never scheduled. runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'macos-26-xlarge' }}. CAN ANY GITHUB-HOSTED macOS RUNNER RUN THE REAL E4B QAT REFERENCE? Effectively NO.
- macos-26 (free, M1, 3 vCPU, 7 GB): model alone is 5.15 GB before the 16K q4_0 KV cache and OS/runner overhead. The lane's own default floor (min_memory_gb=12) excludes it. NO.
- macos-26-xlarge (M2 Pro, 5 vCPU, 14 GB): RAM-wise YES (holds 5.15 GB + 16K q4_0 KV), but it is 2 GB below the documented 16 GB M1 reference, is billed per-minute even on public repos, and per the PR body larger runners require an ORG-OWNED repository — den-run-ai/askme is user-owned, so a dispatch with defaults would queue forever for a runner that can never be allocated. Practically NO on this repo today.
- macos-26-large (Intel, 12 vCPU, 30 GB): plenty of RAM but x86 with no Metal, so `--require-apple-silicon` in the hardware gate would fail it before the download. NO.
True 16 GB Apple Silicon parity requires a third-party arm64 label (Depot depot-macos-26, WarpBuild warp-macos-26-arm64-6x, Blaze, Bitrise) or self-hosted Tart/Tartelet, passed via the `runner` input with min_memory_gb=16.
